authorship: AI-authored and AI-graded by isolated evaluator. No implementation, prior questions, or prior gold consulted. Only public README API contract and runner mechanics were read.

scoring.aggregate_rule: A substantive turn is fully passed only when every applicable axis passes. Report axis counts, task completion, blocked turns, and model usage separately. Runtime success is not semantic success. A blocked turn is NOT_OBSERVED, never passed.
scoring.source_rule: Read complete saved answer/result/assessments/citations/review/trace, not just a matching snippet. Compare quotes with frozen corpus. Do not treat source IDs or lexical overlap as proof of entailment.
scoring.usage_rule: At most 6 submitted Agent tasks and 42 model calls under documented 6 decisions plus one review per task. No task retry. Block dependent turns after failed/unknown predecessor.

reference_resolution.pass: Identify the exact intended object(s); retain original and corrected referents when needed; ask which worker on the deliberately ambiguous turn.
reference_resolution.fail: Continue answering for the superseded build, swap original/current referents, or silently choose one worker.

semantic_claims.pass: Every required substantive claim is correct; all additional factual/causal/quantitative claims are entailed or clearly marked as unsupported hypotheses; derived arithmetic is correct.
semantic_claims.fail: Any required substantive claim missing or wrong, invented fact, unjustified cause, or incorrect whole-report conclusion. Partial is descriptive only and does not count as a full semantic pass.

source_grounding.pass: Required claims cite the matching source passages; exact quotations exist in frozen documents and entail their attached claims. Conflicting sources both retained.
source_grounding.fail: Citations missing for material claims, wrong source, fabricated/modified quote, existence-only citation without entailment, or one-sided contradiction handling.

retrieval_coverage.pass: Trace/search/read evidence includes all minimal needed frozen source documents and applicable passages before report. Score separately from conclusions.
retrieval_coverage.fail: A necessary passage was not retrieved/read. An available hit that is ignored in final reasoning still passes coverage but can fail semantics.

false_refusal.pass: Answer available requested fields and calculations; withhold only missing or genuinely disputed conclusions; clarification only for genuine ambiguity.
false_refusal.fail: Claims answerable facts are unavailable, broadly refuses despite evidence, or fabricates an answer instead of a necessary bounded abstention.

constraint_scope.pass: Chinese answer with intact build/machine identifiers and units; all claims limited to local synthetic supplied evidence; no production quality, rollout eligibility, or external factual inference.
constraint_scope.fail: External/production extrapolation, language/units that materially impede the requested answer, or violation of persistent no-invention/conflict constraints.

required_claims: Larch-12 p95 latency is 72 ms, at or below the 80 ms threshold.
Larch-12 failure rate is 0.33% (2/600, approximately 0.3333%), at or below the 0.5% threshold.
Both conditions pass; therefore this synthetic local acceptance gate passes.
larch-t1.answerability: Fully answerable, no clarification or refusal warranted.

larch-t2.reference: User correction replaces Larch-12 with Larch-14 for the same two-metric question; no state patch supplies that correction.
required_claims: Larch-14 p95 latency is 96 ms, above the 80 ms threshold; latency fails.
Larch-14 failure rate is 0.17% (1/600, approximately 0.1667%), below the 0.5% threshold; failure rate passes.
The combined gate fails because of latency.
forbidden_claims: Failure-rate improvement compensates for missing the latency limit.
larch-t2.answerability: Fully answerable from corrected target; correction is sufficiently explicit.

larch-t3.reference: It refers to corrected Larch-14; the first version means Larch-12.
required_claims: Current Larch-14 latency 96 ms is 16 ms above the 80 ms threshold.
Larch-14 latency is 24 ms higher/slower than Larch-12, so latency worsened.
allowed_optional_claims: Would need a 16 ms reduction to meet the threshold.
forbidden_claims: Its latency is 72 ms or is 8 ms below the threshold.
A statistically significant regression is established.
larch-t3.answerability: Fully answerable; prior correction and first turn make referents clear.

cedar-t1.reference: Overall CP-31 run latency, not one worker.
required_claims: Acceptance limit is overall p95 at most 150 ms.
Bench notebook records 162 ms, which would fail the limit.
Dashboard export records 147 ms, which would pass the limit.
Both cover same CP-31/window and conflict; neither is authoritative/superseding; cannot establish a unique overall pass/fail from supplied records.
forbidden_claims: Definitive overall pass or failure without qualification.
One source wins because it is a dashboard/notebook or presumed newer.
cedar-t1.answerability: The conflict and conditional outcomes are answerable; unique overall pass/fail is legitimately unresolved.

cedar-t2.reference: Both Vela-east and Vela-west, same CP-31 local replay.
required_claims: Average electrical power was not measured for Vela-east.
Average electrical power was not measured for Vela-west.
No power-meter/energy measurements exist for CP-31, so supplied evidence does not support deciding which worker consumed less power or was more energy efficient.

conditional_sources.04_node_inventory.md: Required if the answer cites 65 W/95 W ratings; must state ratings are not measured mean power.

allowed_optional_claims: Vela-east adapter rating is 65 W and Vela-west is 95 W; these do not answer the requested mean operating power or support an efficiency ranking.
forbidden_claims: Mean powers are 65 W and 95 W.
Vela-east is more efficient simply because its adapter rating or latency is lower.
cedar-t2.answerability: A bounded missing-field answer is required, not an unsupported numerical answer. This is not a false refusal if it explains missing data for both workers.

cedar-t3.reference: The previous turn names two peer workers. That machine has no uniquely specified referent.
required_claims: Ask user to specify whether they mean Vela-east or Vela-west before selecting a machine-specific pass/fail.
allowed_optional_claims: May provide explicitly conditional values for both workers while asking which one: Vela-east 138 ms passes 150 ms; Vela-west 171 ms fails. Such factual additions must cite bench notebook plus brief.
forbidden_claims: Treats aggregate CP-31 conflict as if it answered this worker-specific ambiguity.
States node latency unavailable even though both values exist.
cedar-t3.answerability: Deliberately ambiguous; clarification is warranted and is not false refusal. Tool/agent_state may be recorded separately; semantic clarification is the essential requirement.
